text:
maria: heads-up — acme bank POC tomorrow. they want streaming via our SDK + function/tool calls mid-stream and structured JSON output. worried about partial tool payloads and rehydration. can someone outline a simple pattern i can share with their eng team? cc @sam @ashwin

sam: do they prefer SSE or websocket? which language stack?

maria: python server sending events -> our SDK over sse. they specifically want to call a search tool mid-stream, return structured JSON, then continue tokens to the client.

ashwin: we do have a recommended pattern. short version: emit explicit tool_call_start/tool_call_chunk/tool_call_end events with a call_id, buffer chunks server-side until end, then emit a tool_result event referencing call_id. client correlates and resumes stream.

sam: example (pseudo):
```py
with client.stream(model="rwd-large", mode="sse") as s:
    for chunk in s:
        if chunk.type == "tool_call_start":
            call_id = chunk.call_id
            buf = []
        elif chunk.type == "tool_call_chunk":
            buf.append(chunk.text)
        elif chunk.type == "tool_call_end":
            tool_payload = "".join(buf)
            result = tools.search(tool_payload)
            s.emit_tool_result(call_id, json=result)
        else:
            print(chunk.text, end="")
```

ashwin: that emit_tool_result helper sends an SSE event `event: tool_result` with body {call_id, result}. clients can treat that as an atomic structured message. we added this to sample-client v1.12.

leo: quick security question from their GRC: can streaming use ephemeral creds and still meet SOC2? also they want to know about KMS for any stored tool outputs.

ashwin: yes. for presales we recommend STS short-lived tokens (<=1h) + ip allowlist for the POC. hosted tier supports customer-managed keys on enterprise plans; dedicated/private can integrate customer KMS. for now ephemeral tokens + TLS + audit logs should satisfy initial controls. i'll attach the runbook link after.

dev-bot: note: sample-client v1.12 has stream toolcall helpers and `emit_tool_result` API.

maria: the hard part for them is partial JSON across chunks — do we have a tiny repro i can hand them?

sam: yep. general tips: 1) always send a tool_call_end event, 2) include content-length or chunk-index metadata if you can, 3) if payloads may be binary/large, base64 chunk them and set `is_base64:true`, 4) set batch_size=1 on the server for lowest latency while debugging.

ashwin: i'll create a minimal demo repo (python + sample server) and drop a curl/one-liner they can run.

sam: one-liner for them to try quickly (python):
```bash
pip install redwood-sdk && python - <<'PY'
from redwood import Client
c=Client(api_key="$TEMP_KEY")
with c.stream(model="rwd-large", mode="sse") as s:
    for e in s:
        print(e, end="")
PY
```

maria: perfect — can you paste the demo link in this thread when ready?

ashwin: will do. also pinging @leo if they need a short security note for the SOW.

leo: i'll prepare a one-page blurb on ephemeral creds + kms options. thanks.

maria: amazing, appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
